name: Baked gem squash
summary: Halved gem squash boiled until tender, then filled with butter and creamed sweetcorn and baked until bubbling.
about: Gem squash — small, round and dark green, about the size of a tennis ball — is a vegetable South Africans grow up on and one that is hard to find in many other countries. Filled with butter and sweetcorn, it is a side children happily eat straight from the shell.
steps: Cut each squash in half around its middle and scoop out the seeds with a spoon.
Put the halves cut side down in a large pot of salted boiling water, cover and simmer over medium heat for 12–15 minutes, until the flesh is soft when pierced. Drain them upside down.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Set the halves cut side up on a baking tray and put a knob of butter, a pinch of salt and some pepper in each hollow.
Fill the hollows with creamed sweetcorn and top with the cheese, if using.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top. Serve in the shell with a spoon for scooping out the flesh.
